question_details.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve positively if Google implements an explanation feature for ads in their Google Ads platform before January 1, 2026.  Google must have implemented this feature across the platform for all users, not only in certain formats (such as only in Google Search) or as an A/B test.  Google announcements or credible media reports may suffice as a resolution source.

"Explanations" will be considered any explanation for advertisement selection which indicates decisive charactaristics of the advertiser or of the user.  It is not necessary for this explation to be comprehensive (Google may withhold some key information in decision-making), nor must the explanation be "true" (regarding how the algorithm actually makes decisions), as either are in principle not verifiable

**Modelling transcription with explainable AI uncovers context-specific epigenetic gene regulation at promoters and gene bodies**
This study develops deep neural network (DNN) models—including multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost), and linear regression—to predict RNA Polymerase II (Pol-II) occupancy from ChIP-seq data, with MLPs selected for their high performance, efficiency, and interpretability potential via explainable AI (XAI) methods. Direct transcriptional targets (genes with significant transcriptional changes after acute protein degradation, p-adjusted < 0.05) were compared to random genes (p-adjusted > 0.05), with 50 balanced subsamples per test split preserving the 6–28% target proportion. Mean absolute SHAP values were averaged across 50 repeats to reduce bias. SHAP values, which reconstruct model predictions with local accuracy and consistency, enabled gene-by-gene comparison of regulatory feature importance. In contrast to linear regression, which provides only global insights, SHAP offers individual gene-level resolution, revealing context-specific regulatory patterns. Startups can implement XAI by mapping high-impact decisions (e.g., loan approvals, health recommendations), applying post-hoc tools like SHAP and LIME with caveats, integrating explanation dashboards and APIs, maintaining versioned documentation, and testing explanations with real users. summary: Across all experts, there is strong consensus that Google has not yet implemented, announced, or previewed a platform-wide, user-facing ad explanation feature comparable to Facebook's 'Why am I seeing this ad?' and that the short time left before the January 1, 2026, deadline makes such a deployment extremely unlikely. Experts from fields including AdTech, Data Privacy, US Tech Policy, Computer Science (HCI and XAI), Marketing, and Law (Data Privacy and Consumer Protection) each highlight mounting competitive and regulatory pressures (GDPR, EU AI Act, US FTC guidance, and actions by Meta and OpenAI) pushing toward ad transparency and explainability. However, they universally note the lack of credible announcements, public beta tests, leaks, or visible development signaling an imminent full-platform rollout by Google. While technical feasibility is not the limiting factor, experts stress Google's business incentives to maintain some opacity in targeting logic, the historically slow adoption of such features, and the operational challenges of global feature launches. All agree that absent a last-minute PR or regulatory crisis forcing Google’s hand, minor incremental updates or restricted pilots are the most likely outcomes in the near term. Final probability estimates for the question resolving 'Yes' are uniformly low, ranging from 3% to 25%, with most clustering between 8% and 18%. The aggregate expert view is that, although explainable ads are likely in Google’s medium-term roadmap under mounting external pressure, the chance of full implementation for all users before 2026 is very small.
